1. Primary Request and Intent:
Build a complete Node.js invoicing system over multiple iterations. User requested: (1) invoice creation with line items and validation, (2) line management (add/remove), (3) sequential invoice numbering, (4) text rendering, (5) line-level and tier-based discounts, (6) VAT calculation per line, (7) customer ID normalization, (8) date utilities with UTC arithmetic, and (9) payment recording functionality.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
- Functional error handling via ok()/fail() pattern from result.js
- Money as integers in cents (no fractional amounts, use roundCents() for calculations)
- Customer ID normalization (trim + uppercase for consistent lookups)
- Date handling as YYYY-MM-DD strings with UTC-only arithmetic
- Tier-based automatic discounts (gold: 5%, silver: 2.5%, standard: 0%)
- VAT calculation per line (before being summed), with per-line rounding using roundCents()
- Invoice status transitions: draft → issued → partially_paid/paid
- Sequential invoice numbering per calendar year (INV-YYYY-0001 format)
- Immutability: never mutate input arguments, return new objects/arrays

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - src/errors.js
     - Centralized error codes with human-readable messages
     - Added: NOT_ISSUED, OVERPAYMENT, DATE_INVALID, NO_LINES, QTY_INVALID, DISCOUNT_INVALID, CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND, UNKNOWN_SKU, AMOUNT_INVALID, CUSTOMER_INVALID, LINE_NOT_FOUND
   
   - src/invoices.js
     - createInvoice({ customerId, issueDate, lines }): validates customer (normalized ID), date (YYYY-MM-DD), lines array, quantity (positive integer), discount (0-100), SKU existence; applies tier discount if no explicit discount; returns ok(invoice) or fail(code)
     - addLine(invoice, { sku, qty, discountPercent }): adds new line or increases existing; applies tier discount if no explicit discount; validates qty and discount; returns ok(newInvoice)
     - removeLine(invoice, sku): removes line; errors if NOT_DRAFT, LINE_NOT_FOUND, or would remove last line; returns ok(newInvoice)
     - issueInvoice(invoice, existingNumbers): assigns invoice number and changes status to 'issued'
     - lineTotal(line): qty × unitPrice
     - lineVat(line): calculates VAT on discounted amount, rounded per-line with roundCents()
     - invoiceTotals(invoice): returns { subtotal, discount, vat, total } where total = subtotal - discount + vat, clamped at 0
   
   - src/customers.js
     - normalizeId(id): trims whitespace and converts to uppercase
     - getCustomer(id): normalizes input before lookup
     - TIER_DISCOUNTS: { gold: 5, silver: 2.5, standard: 0 }
   
   - src/dates.js
     - isValidDate(dateStr): validates YYYY-MM-DD format and real dates (including leap years)
     - addDays(date, n): adds/subtracts days using UTC; handles month/year boundaries
     - daysBetween(a, b): calculates whole days (b - a) in UTC
   
   - src/numbering.js
     - nextInvoiceNumber(existingNumbers, issueDate): generates INV-YYYY-NNNN with year-reset counter
   
   - src/render.js
     - renderInvoiceText(invoice): renders plain-text invoice with lines, VAT, and Total; all currency via formatEuros()
   
   - src/money.js
     - roundCents(x): banker's rounding (half to even)
     - formatEuros(cents): formats as €X,XXX.XX with thousands separators
   
   - src/result.js
     - ok(value): returns { ok: true, value }
     - fail(error, details?): returns { ok: false, error, details? }

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Test expectation mismatches when VAT rounding was added: discount tests didn't account for tier discounts being applied; had to recalculate expected VAT values using roundCents() to match actual rounding behavior
   - Fixed by updating test assertions to use actual calculated values rather than incorrect manual math
   - User feedback: none explicitly, but implicit guidance was to handle money correctly (use roundCents), validate all inputs, and never mutate arguments

5. Problem Solving:
   - Solved sequential invoice numbering per year with counter reset
   - Solved VAT calculation: computed per line on discounted amount, then summed (not a percentage of invoice total)
   - Solved tier discount application: only applied when no explicit discountPercent provided; explicit discount (even 0) always wins
   - Solved date validation: using UTC-only arithmetic to avoid timezone issues
   - Solved ID normalization: applied at boundary (getCustomer, createInvoice) to ensure consistent internal state

   - "Invoice numbers. Decision: an invoice number is INV-<year>-<counter>... Add nextInvoiceNumber(existingNumbers, issueDate)... issueInvoice(invoice, existingNumbers)..."
   - "Add renderInvoiceText(invoice)... returns a plain-text invoice: a first line with the invoice number (or DRAFT if it has none), a line with the customer's name, one line per invoice line... last line starting with 'Total: '. Decision: every amount we show to a customer goes through formatEuros()..."
   - "Line discounts. A line may now carry discountPercent... createInvoice and addLine accept it... a value outside 0-100 or that isn't a number returns DISCOUNT_INVALID... A line's discount is its line total times discountPercent / 100... invoiceTotals now returns { subtotal, discount, total }... Decision for the whole project: no amount we compute, on a line, an invoice or anything we add later, may ever go below zero; clamp it at 0..."
   - "Customer tiers. Every customer has a tier... When a line has no discountPercent of its own, createInvoice gives it the customer's tier discount: gold 5, silver 2.5, standard 0. A line's own discountPercent (even 0) always wins... Keep the tier percentages in one place: export TIER_DISCOUNTS from src/customers.js..."
   - "VAT. Every line has a vatRate... Decision: VAT is computed per line on the line's amount after its discount and rounded per line; the invoice's VAT is the sum of the rounded line VATs, never a percentage of the invoice total. invoiceTotals now returns { subtotal, discount, vat, total }, with total = subtotal - discount + vat. Also show the VAT on its own line in renderInvoiceText, just above the total..."
   - "Customer IDs reach us in mixed case and with stray spaces... Add normalizeId(id)... Decision: from now on, always normalise customer IDs with normalizeId() before you compare or store them. Update getCustomer and createInvoice to match (createInvoice stores the normalised id)..."
